name: 2s/10s Yield Curve Inversion: S&P 500 Peak Lag & Drawdown
description: Analyzes each 2s/10s yield curve inversion event (spread crosses below zero). For each inversion: shows the date, the subsequent S&P 500 peak date, the lag in days from inversion to peak, and the maximum drawdown from that peak. Uses FRED T10Y2Y spread and SP500 index.
source:
# 2s/10s Yield Curve Inversion → S&P 500 Peak & Drawdown Analysis
# Detects each inversion event (spread crosses below zero), then tracks
# the subsequent S&P 500 peak and maximum drawdown from that peak.
#
# Key insight: inversions are rare (~5-7 since 1976). For each one we
# capture the S&P 500 running max AFTER the inversion, the date of that
# peak, and the worst drawdown from that peak — all within a 504-bar
# (~2 year) forward window.

# --- Data ---
src = study_assets()
ts = index().value

# 2s/10s spread from FRED (daily)
spread_raw = economic_indicators(series_id="T10Y2Y")
spread = ffill(spread_raw.result)

# S&P 500 index level from FRED (daily)
spx_raw = economic_indicators(series_id="SP500")
spx = ffill(spx_raw.result)

# --- Inversion Detection ---
# Inversion = spread crosses below zero
inversion_start = crossunder(spread, 0)

# Track inversion regime for shading
in_inversion = hold_until(inversion_start, crossover(spread, 0))

# --- Forward-Looking Metrics at Each Inversion ---
# S&P 500 level at inversion
spx_at_inv = valuewhen(inversion_start, spx, 0)

# Timestamp at inversion
ts_at_inv = valuewhen(inversion_start, ts, 0)

# S&P 500 peak in the 504 trading days (~2 years) AFTER each bar
# We use a lead-based approach: the max of the next 504 bars
# agg with lead: compute rolling max of future values
# Forward max: shift spx backward (lead) and take rolling max
# Simpler: use the << operator to look ahead and find the peak

# Forward running max over next 504 bars (look-ahead, acceptable for research)
spx_lead_max = agg(spx, 504, AggregationType.Max)

# The peak date: use arg_minmax expanding to get the timestamp of the max
# But we need per-cycle. Instead, capture the rolling max timestamp.
# arg_minmax gives the timestamp of the min/max of the ENTIRE expanding series.
# For per-event analysis, we capture the peak level and use datetime_diff.

# Peak S&P 500 in the 504 bars after each inversion
spx_peak = valuewhen(inversion_start, spx_lead_max, 0)

# To find the peak DATE, we create a flag where spx equals its 504-bar max
# and capture the timestamp of that bar nearest to the inversion
# Alternative: use the expanding arg_minmax and capture at inversion

# Track the expanding all-time high and its date
spx_ath = agg(spx, 504, AggregationType.Max)
is_new_high = spx == spx_ath
new_high_ts = valuewhen(is_new_high, ts, 0)

# At each inversion, the peak date is the last new-high date
# within the forward window. We approximate by finding when
# spx reaches the 504-bar max level.
# Better approach: use arg_minmax
peak_info = arg_minmax(expanding=True)(spx)
peak_date_expanding = peak_info.max_loc

# Capture peak date at each inversion event
peak_date_at_inv = valuewhen(inversion_start, peak_date_expanding, 0)

# Lag in days from inversion to the expanding peak
lag_to_peak = datetime_diff(unit=TimeDiffUnit.days)(ts_at_inv, peak_date_at_inv)

# --- Drawdown from Peak ---
# Running max of S&P 500 (expanding)
spx_running_max = agg(spx, 10000, AggregationType.Max)
# Drawdown from running max at each bar
dd_from_max = (spx - spx_running_max) / spx_running_max
# Worst drawdown in 756 bars (~3 years) after each bar
worst_dd_fwd = agg(dd_from_max, 756, AggregationType.Min)
# Capture worst drawdown at each inversion
max_dd_at_inv = valuewhen(inversion_start, worst_dd_fwd, 0)

# --- Sparse Event Series (emit only at inversion dates) ---
evt_inv_date = where(inversion_start, ts_at_inv)
evt_peak_date = where(inversion_start, peak_date_at_inv)
evt_lag = where(inversion_start, lag_to_peak.value)
evt_spx = where(inversion_start, spx_at_inv)
evt_dd = where(inversion_start, max_dd_at_inv)

# --- Output 1: Event Markers on Inversion Dates ---
event_marker(
    schema=EventMarkerSchema(
        title='Yield Curve Inversion',
        icon=Icon.AlertTriangleIcon,
        schemas=[
            ColumnSpec(title='2s/10s Spread', dp=2, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Hero),
            ColumnSpec(title='S&P 500 Level', dp=0, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Subtitle),
            ColumnSpec(table_is_filter=True, table_visible=False)
        ]
    )
)(spread, spx, inversion_start)

# --- Output 2: Context Chart — 2s/10s Spread with Inversion Shading ---
inv_band = nz(where(in_inversion, 1.0), 0.0)

xy_lines(
    title='When Does the Yield Curve Invert?',
    y_axis_label='Spread (%)',
    category='Yield Curve Inversion Analysis',
    order=1,
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name='2s/10s Spread', color=Color.Blue),
        LineSeriesSpec(name='Inverted', color=Color.Red, is_band=True)
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0.0, title='Zero', color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash)
    ])
)(ts, spread, inv_band)

# --- Output 3: Per-Inversion Table ---
# Each inversion emits one row with: date, peak date, lag, S&P level, max drawdown
summary_table(
    mode=TableMode.standard,
    category='Yield Curve Inversion Analysis',
    order=2,
    layout=SummaryTableLayout(
        title='Each Inversion → Subsequent S&P 500 Peak & Drawdown',
        row_size=1, col_size=5,
        col_headers=['Inversion Date', 'S&P 500 Peak Date', 'Days to Peak', 'S&P at Inversion', 'Max Drawdown from Peak'],
        cells=[
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.DateFormat),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.DateFormat),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=2, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.IntegerFormat, dp=0),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=3, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat, dp=0),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=4, grid_agg=AggregationType.Last,
                       type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1,
                       grid_color=Color.Red)
        ]
    )
)(evt_inv_date, evt_peak_date, evt_lag, evt_spx, evt_dd)
